clue.text: State tax one is able to afford

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
I is the Roman numeral for one
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A complaint that one can only just pay the taxes levied by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afford' is a link word here; the Vatican City is a sovereign state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican City is the smallest independent country in the world, run by the Pope.

clue.text: I'll not hesitate to leave

indicators.note: not means the letters of I'll are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to vacillate is to waver or hesitate
I'll without the apostrophe gives the letters I, L, L

explanation.surface: A determined person says they will go without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'I'll' is ignored, as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a room or post is to move out and leave it empty.

clue.text: Common fund split into ten

indicators.note: split means broken up, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shared pot is divided into ten parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' rearranges INTO TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is an investment scheme where members share a pot, the last survivor taking all.

clue.text: Vegetable produce in yard an eye-opener

indicators.note: in means the word for produce sits inside the yard

parts.note: a court is an enclosed yard
to get is to produce or obtain

indicators.note: the opener of the eye is its first letter

explanation.surface: Vegetables grown in someone's yard prove surprisingly impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' looks like a surprise; here 'opener' takes the first letter of 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette is a small marrow, known in American English as zucchini.

clue.text: Blue, having no money

explanation.surface: Someone is sad because they are broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are risqué, close to indecency; someone close to poverty lives frugally, both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Exotic fruit from tree about to fill the void

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another to fill it, so goes in the middle

parts.note: a gap is a void

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the tree is written backwards

parts.note: a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: A rare fruit picked from a tree, said to satisfy emptiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a reversal signal here, not 'roughly', and 'the void' is a gap rather than empty space in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The genipap is a tropical American tree yielding an edible orange-sized fruit.

clue.text: From anchorage, explorers move on

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run across these two words

explanation.surface: Explorers set off again from a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'anchorage' and the start of 'explorers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee, or gee up, is a call urging a horse forward.

clue.text: A superior person, the French count, possibly

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or upper-class person
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Describing a grand French nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link; 'count' is the title, defined by example, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is an aristocrat, one of the titled nobility.

clue.text: State that's put up one city

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial state, as in pomp and state

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters are written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A state establishes a single city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses IE to give EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Working man accepts an' apprentice — that's nice!

indicators.note: accepts means the farm worker takes in the learner letter

parts.note: a peasant is a farm labourer
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A labourer takes on an apprentice and is pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an'' is a link word in dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant is agreeable or enjoyable.

clue.text: Cleans out scruffy government office

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cleaner tidies up a shabby government building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleans out' looks like the action; it is the fodder that 'scruffy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the building where a foreign country's consul works.

clue.text: Ice-cream takes a lot of money, with cream in the middle

parts.note: a bomb is slang for a large sum of money, as in cost a bomb

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word cream is taken

explanation.surface: A dessert costs a fortune and has a creamy centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'costs a bomb' is British slang for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dessert moulded into a dome shape.

clue.text: Drawing difficult? That's not. right

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out of the word

parts.note: trying means difficult or wearing

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that drawing is hard, then corrects themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but it means drawing level in a match, as in a tied game.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides that are drawing are level, with scores equal, so they are tying.

clue.text: Uninteresting column accepted, by foreign news agency

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: TASS is the Russian (formerly Soviet) news agency
a stele is an upright stone column or slab

explanation.surface: A dull newspaper column is taken by a news agency abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the stone pillar STELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without flavour or interest is bland and insipid.

clue.text: In the last resort, the horse can run wild

indicators.note: letters that run wild are scattered out of order

explanation.surface: In a crisis, a horse may bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run wild' rearranges THE HORSE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet anchor was a ship's large spare anchor, so figuratively a final reliance.

clue.text: Metronome of use for this unconventional youth?

definitions.text: Metronome of use for this unconventional youth?

parts.words: Metronome of use for this unconventional youth?
parts.note: a metronome produces a regular beat, so it generates beats, and the clue jokes that this would suit the 1950s American literary youth movement

explanation.surface: A metronome might help a group of rebellious young people keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1950s Beat movement of Kerouac and Ginsberg is punned on as a group that generates beats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beats were a 1950s group of American writers rejecting mainstream values.

clue.text: Vigilance required to 'give beer right head

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Being watchful demands giving beer the right amount of froth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests froth on beer; it is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and on guard is a state of wakeful attention.

clue.text: Alert everyone in the place

parts.note: all means everyone
there means in that place

explanation.surface: Everyone present is wide awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally sharp and quick-witted is all there.

clue.text: Legal nicety left theatre low, utterly ruined

indicators.note: something utterly ruined is wrecked into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A production left a theatre in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly ruined' rearranges LEFT THEATRE LOW, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping to the exact wording of a rule rather than its spirit is a legal technicality.

clue.text: Put the finger on Tom and. Edward

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the fairy tale
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Accusing two people, Tom and Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the finger on' suggests informing on someone; it means touched with a digit.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch or leaf through something with a digit is to have handled it.

clue.text: Planes streak, 'ardly visible

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows the H dropped, so the letter H is missing

parts.note: a hairline is a very thin streak or line

explanation.surface: Aircraft leave a faint streak in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ardly is hardly with its H dropped, a cockney pronunciation, so HAIRLINE loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company operating a fleet of aircraft.

clue.text: The king, when it's. dark, is another man

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess
night is the time when it is dark

explanation.surface: The king is a different person after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece; the king clue sits beside another chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is a chess piece, as is the king.

clue.text: Staff — their heart not in it, left out of meal

indicators.note: the word their loses its middle, leaving only its first and last letters
out of means the letter for left is removed from the meal

parts.note: luncheon is a formal word for a midday meal

explanation.surface: Staff are half-hearted after being left out of lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their heart not in it' leaves T and R from THEIR; 'out of' drops L from LUNCHEON to give UNCHEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club or baton carried by a police officer.

clue.text: Female animal and 'er fawn.

parts.note: a cow is a female animal
'er is her with the h dropped

explanation.surface: A cow and her young deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' suggests a young deer; here it is the verb to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn or grovel is to shrink in fear or servility.

clue.text: Start to 'turn old city into a more modern one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word turn is used

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
in is a short form of into

explanation.surface: An instruction to convert an ancient city into a modern one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the biblical city, is a crossword staple; Turin is the more modern Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is an industrial Italian city, far younger than ancient Ur.

clue.text: Shove 6 up, finally changing: direction

indicators.note: the last letter, a compass point, swaps for another compass point
in a down clue answer read upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is noble

explanation.surface: Push the answer to 6 upwards, then turn at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NOBLE to ELBON; 'finally changing direction' swaps its last letter N (north) for W (west).
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to push someone aside with the arm, to jostle or barge.

clue.text: Rash man in NZ port losing head and heart to baggage

indicators.note: in means the word for man goes inside the port
the port's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Dunedin is a port city in New Zealand
he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the central letter of baggage is added on

explanation.surface: A reckless traveller in a New Zealand harbour loses his head and his heart to his luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the port's first letter D; 'baggage' is not luggage here, it only supplies its central G.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heedless of warnings is to act rashly and carelessly.

clue.text: Employ American expertise primarily

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of expertise is used

explanation.surface: Hire someone for their American know-how.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to put it to work.

clue.text: Back, after tip, a runner that doesn't. start

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the word for tip

parts.note: the end is the tip of something

indicators.note: the runner loses its opening letter

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A gambler backs a horse after a tip, but it fails to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests betting on a horse; here it means support, and 'tip' is the end rather than a racing hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a plan or person publicly is to give it your backing.

clue.text: In this regard, he could give us the, creeps

indicators.note: in this answer the letters of the ghost appear with its last pair moved to the front

parts.words: he could give us the, creeps
parts.note: a spectre is a ghost, which could give anyone the creeps

explanation.surface: In this respect, someone frightening could make us shudder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this' tells you the answer contains the letters of SPECTRE, with RE moved from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high esteem is to regard or admire them.
